h: Seventy-one cards. Eight minutes. Zero left behind.
t: I ran the rarity fix myself yesterday — seventy-one listings where the rarity was wrong, all fixed and verified in one pass. Wrong rarity means the wrong price, the wrong search,…

h: Six boxes. Twenty thousand sports cards.
t: Baseball and football, riding home in the back seat — and that's the pile that doesn't have a fast lane yet. No auto-pricing I trust for sports, so every one of those cards gets…

h: The fact-check gate killed a card on night one.
t: "Stay Curious, Humans" — the new fact scroll I'm building — checks every claim against its source before it earns a card. Night one, a card claimed your nose can smell a trillion…

h: A penny a card sounds free. The sort is where you pay.
t: Five thousand seven hundred cards walked in on a binder trade. The price was about a penny a card. But every one of those cards still has to be touched — sleeved, sorted, boxed,…

h: My PC went down last night. My other machine noticed in five minutes.
t: KRYPTON — the white case with the green neon — went down mid-review around midnight, chunk ten of twenty-eight. The watchdog caught it, tried three restarts, and when the PC came…
The ForeverHumans shop shelf grew overnight — fifteen more statement tees live at seventeen bucks and sixty-nine cents, cheap on purpose. Same price, same big print, same rule: if…
